title: Report: Guardian Interview Reveals New GTA 6 Gameplay Details From Rockstar North Visit
description: The Guardian's Keza MacDonald toured Rockstar North and reported new gameplay details for Grand Theft Auto VI, including protagonist Jason Duval eating a hot dog while holding a beer and a donut, realistic liquid physics when running with a six-pack, and insights into the studio's Miami research tri
youtubeTitle: Guardian Interview Reveals GTA 6 Gameplay Details: Eating, Drinking, Physics
socialHook: The Guardian's Keza MacDonald visited Rockstar North and saw Jason Duval eat a hot dog while holding a beer and a donut.

sections.heading: Guardian Interview Reveals Gameplay Details
paragraphs: The Guardian journalist Keza MacDonald visited Rockstar North in Edinburgh and described the game as "gratuitously, absurdly detailed," according to RockstarINTEL's summary of the article. During a gameplay demonstration, protagonist Jason Duval was shown eating a hot dog while simultaneously sipping a beer in one hand and taking a bite from a donut in the other, illustrating the game's multitasking mechanics.

MacDonald also noted that when Jason runs while carrying a six-pack of beer, the case moves into the crook of his arm with the liquid realistically sloshing inside the bottles. Studio head Rob Nelson reportedly became briefly upset during a robbery scene because the placement of a security guard's feet "didn't look right," highlighting the team's obsession with minute details.

sections.heading: Rockstar North Development Insights
paragraphs: Nelson reminisced about early production research trips to Miami, including late-night visits to nightclubs, a hangover-fueled day at a Floridian racetrack, ride-alongs with police, and time spent in unusual bars — experiences that likely inspired in-game locations such as the Rusty Anchor bar.

The Guardian's Saturday Magazine is expected to publish more details from the visit later this week. Additionally, RockstarINTEL noted that broadband provider Virgin Media O2 recorded a record-breaking traffic peak due to GTA 6's 200GB+ preload rollout, though that is a separate development.
